bullets.title: MU: Historic Beat & 16 Strategic Customer Agreements Transform Business Model
bullets.body: Micron reported F3Q26 revenue of $41.46B (vs. consensus ~$35.9B) and EPS of $25.11 (vs. ~$20.86), with gross margin of 84.9% (+320bps above consensus). F4Q guidance of $50B revenue and $31 EPS (both ~15-22% above Street) with ~86% GM. The headline catalyst: 16 Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs) covering ~20% of DRAM and ~33% of NAND volume, representing $100B+ minimum cumulative revenue over 5-year take-or-pay terms with upfront cash deposits of $22B; management expects >50% of revenue under SCAs when complete. Supply tightness expected to persist beyond CY27 with no demand/supply balance visibility into 2028. MU committed to returning 100% of excess cash to shareholders starting Dec 9, 2026; FY27 capex guided well above mid-$40Bs. PT range across banks: GS $1,100, MS $1,200, Citi $1,400, Wolfe $1,500, KeyBanc $1,600, JPM $1,540, UBS $1,625. 94% Buy, 0% Sell on Street.

bullets.title: SNDK: NAND Supply Tight Through CY27+; Citi Raises PT to $2,500, Opens 90-Day Upside View
bullets.body: Citi's Asiya Merchant raises SNDK PT to $2,500 (from prior) based on 11x CY27 EPS, citing MU read-through that NAND supply/demand tightness extends beyond CY27. SNDK shares +15-16% in pre-market. SNDK expected to execute same LTSA structure as MU but with significantly lower capex, implying potential for higher re-rating. August investor day flagged as next catalyst for capital return commentary.

bullets.title: INTC: Goldman Sachs Initiates at Neutral, $150 PT; +6.4% Pre-Market
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider initiates Intel at Neutral with a $150 PT (~14% upside from $131.65), citing server CPU demand tailwinds from agentic AI and foundry optionality but noting current valuation already reflects positives. Stock +6.4% in pre-market trading.

bullets.title: AFRM: Morgan Stanley Downgrades to Equal-Weight; Growth Durability Now Priced In
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley downgrades Affirm from Overweight to Equal-Weight, stating the market now properly reflects the durability of growth, funding, and credit quality. AFRM maintains best-in-class fintech profile with stable unit economics, but risk/reward no longer asymmetric. Stock -2.1% pre-market.

bullets.title: META: Business Agent TAM $75B+; Piper Reiterates OW; AI Moderation Acceleration
bullets.body: Piper Sandler reiterates META as top large-cap pick/Overweight, citing the Business Agent launch at Conversations 2026 with $75B+ TAM and the stock trading at ~16x 2027E EPS with minimal agent revenue priced in (likely not scaling until 2027). Separately, META is accelerating replacement of human content moderation with generative AI—already at ~50% replacement YTD, targeting >90% for certain content types by year-end.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS GPU Pricing +20% July 1; E-Commerce Accelerating; JPM Reiterates OW $330 PT
bullets.body: JPM reiterates AMZN Overweight with $330 PT: AWS EC2 Block GPU pricing increases 20% effective July 1, 2026. US e-commerce growth expected to accelerate to +9.6% Y/Y in 2026 vs. +5.4% in 2025, with AMZN holding ~47% US e-com share. Long-term online penetration could reach 40%+ from current ~24%, driven by grocery/CPG. Separately, EU Commission reached preliminary position that AWS should be designated a DMA gatekeeper, with 6-month compliance window if confirmed.

bullets.title: MSFT/AMZN: EU DMA Gatekeeper Preliminary Designation for Cloud Services
bullets.body: EU Commission reached a preliminary position that both AWS and Azure should be designated as DMA gatekeepers for their cloud computing services. Both companies retain the right to exercise their defense; if confirmed, they have six months to ensure full compliance.

bullets.title: NFLX: Wolfe Initiates Outperform at $107 PT; MS Survey Shows Content Lead Intact
bullets.body: Wolfe Research initiates NFLX Outperform at $107 PT (47% upside), arguing 19x 2027 P/E is cheap vs. 87 S&P 500 peers at 20-25x with median 7% rev CAGR vs. NFLX's 15%. YTD performance -22.6% creates entry point. Morgan Stanley's 16th annual streaming survey confirms NFLX leads net retention (+18 score), pricing power intact (~$20/month seen as great buy with room to $30+), and ad-tier adoption rising to 26%.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Sky Near £1.6B Deal to Acquire ITV Media & Entertainment Business
bullets.body: Sky (Comcast-owned) is close to agreeing terms to buy ITV's Media & Entertainment business for approximately £1.6B (~$2.2B), with an earn-out portion of ~£200M. ITV Studios would separately acquire Love Productions. Transaction could be announced within weeks; deal aims to create a UK streaming competitor to global platforms.

bullets.title: DASH/CART: Oppenheimer Raises PTs; Survey Data Points to 2Q GTV Upside
bullets.body: Oppenheimer reiterates Outperform on DASH with $235 PT: contribution profit analysis suggests 2026-27 EBITDA ~10% above Street, lower gas prices are a dual tailwind (demand + $50M gas subsidy freed up), and proprietary survey confirms DoorDash dominance. CART PT raised to $60 (from $55): Apptopia MAU regression implies 2Q GTV +15% vs. Street +12%, and survey shows Amazon Grocery has no material impact on Instacart.

bullets.title: CHTR: UBS Sees Accelerating 2Q Broadband Losses; Pricing and Political Ads Support H2
bullets.body: UBS maintains Neutral on Charter, modeling 2Q broadband subscriber losses of 166K (vs. -116K year-ago) and 526K full-year losses, with revenue -2.4% and EBITDA -2.7% in 2Q vs. Street's -1.7%/-1.4%. Management planning summer broadband price increase to support H2 ARPU; political ad spending provides high-margin H2 lift. Full-year FCF modeled at $5.1B with ~$4B in buybacks (~22% of market cap).

bullets.title: GLW: JPM Flags Panel Pricing Correction Expected in July; 2H26 Demand Risk Building
bullets.body: JPM warns that LCD TV panel prices, flat m/m in June, are expected to decline -1.6% m/m in July as Chinese and South Korean TV makers cut 2Q26 purchasing plans and shift to requesting price cuts. Panel prices are already down 15 consecutive months Y/Y (-4.7% in June). 2H26 depth of downturn depends on supply discipline and consumer demand recovery.

bullets.title: FIG: JPM Neutral; Config 2026 AI Roadmap Positive But Near-Term Gross Margin Pressure
bullets.body: JPM maintains Neutral on Figma after Config 2026, praising AI agent-assisted tools (Code Layers, Motion, Shaders) that deepen engagement but noting new features will not incur credit costs during beta—deferring monetization and likely pressuring near-term gross margins. Management reaffirmed full-year operating margin targets with no planned price increases.

bullets.title: BABA: Falls to 16-Month Low on Anthropic 'Distillation Attack' Accusations
bullets.body: Anthropic alleges Alibaba used 25,000 fraudulent accounts to generate 28.8M exchanges with Claude AI (April–June 2026), calling it the largest distillation attack by a Chinese company on its systems. BABA shares fell 4.4% in Asia trading to lowest since February 2025, already under pressure from AI credibility doubts and weak China consumption.

bullets.title: WDC/STX: Rallying on MU Read-Through; Memory Oligopoly Pricing Power Highlighted
bullets.body: WDC +12.4% and STX +10.6% pre-market on MU earnings sympathy. One analyst notes WDC and STX have greater pricing power than in past cycles given HDD oligopoly structure with minimal capex and no China risk, and argues they trade at a 300% P/E premium to SNDK/MU that is deserved given cash flow characteristics.

bullets.title: MU: Retail Poured $868M Into Shares Ahead of Earnings; SNDK $354M
bullets.body: Retail investors bought $868M of MU (5.4 standard deviations above normal) and $354M of SNDK (2.4z) on June 24 despite a 3-day -6% semiconductor sector selloff. MU surged ~14-18% after hours. Memory stocks remain retail's primary AI/datacenter expression.

bullets.title: INTU: Citi Downgrades on AI Displacement Risk; Back-Office Software Preferences Shift
bullets.body: Citi downgrades Intuit on persistent AI bear narrative around competition and disintermediation risk, while elevating BOX, APPN, and NAVN as new top picks. Within the broader software ranking, NOW remains relevant but INTU and PEGA see lowered analyst preferences.

bullets.title: TSLA: BEV Penetration Expected Up 10-20bps in June; Model 3 Lease Price Raised $30/mo
bullets.body: JPM forecasts June US BEV penetration at ~6.0% (up 10-20bps m/m from 5.8%). Tesla raised Model 3 lease prices $30/month to $329 and Cybertruck $100/month to $949. Overall June SAAR expected at 16.2M units, +4.3% Y/Y.

bullets.title: NVDA: Hedgeye Flags Bearish Lower-Highs Signal; Caution as AI Leverage Peaks
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags NVDA as showing lower-highs and bearish trade/trend signals, calling it the 'canary' for the broader semi complex. Separately, UBS notes HF short covering in AI Winners (+1.4 std) and Mag 7 (+1.6 std) after Tuesday's record de-grossing, while gross/net US High Momentum exposure remains at 99th percentile.

bullets.title: WDAY: Monness Upgrades to Buy, $150 PT on Valuation
bullets.body: Monness, Crespi, Hardt & Co. upgrades Workday to Buy from Neutral with a $150 PT (27% upside from $118.09), driven by valuation. FactSet consensus target is $173.56.
